spec: ProgressDesk MS3: durable progress. Named immutable checkpoints, a deterministic recovery packet, and one start operation that reconciles the registered jobs and unresolved actions before it dispatches anything. The checkpoint is an acceleration and recovery aid, never a second authority.

acceptanceConditions: a checkpoint manifest names the project, the journal sequence it was derived from, the definition references in force, the accepted artifact manifest, the tool, skill and domain version references in force, the task and milestone state and the pending actions
a checkpoint is immutable and derived from one recorded event position, and a second checkpoint with the same name is refused

the recovery packet names the current task, the accepted baseline, surviving candidate artifacts, completed actions, unresolved effects, failed checks, remaining work and the allowance, and carries no role transcript or private reasoning
the same checkpoint and the same project produce the same recovery packet

project.start is the only start operation: it reconciles the registered jobs and unresolved actions, establishes a clean execution boundary or returns a typed outcome, and never creates a second controller
a torn final record is recovered and an interior corruption is reported as a blocker instead of a reset to ready
replay performs no model, tool or provider call
a log with a gap in the numbering opens and reads in order
a round that does not deliver is split rather than abandoned
a successful round that changed nothing is a delivery

features.title: Named immutable checkpoints
features.outcome: ProgressDesk can create and list named immutable checkpoints, on command and at a milestone boundary. Each manifest records the project, the journal sequence it was derived from, the definition references in force, the accepted artifact manifest, the tool, skill and domain version references in force, the task and milestone state and the pending actions. A checkpoint is an acceleration and recovery aid, never a second authority: everything in it is derived from the event log and the artifact store.
features.scope: New module src/progressdesk/checkpoints.py and the route table in src/progressdesk/runtime.py. Reuse the existing event log and artifact store; do not create a second store and do not change the event vocabulary.
interfaces: route verb 'checkpoint.create' with params project_id, name -> manifest with keys checkpointId, projectId, name, journalSequence, definitionRefs, acceptedArtifactManifestRef, toolSkillDomainVersionRefs, taskAndMilestoneStateRef, pendingActionRefs, createdAt
a milestone boundary creates a checkpoint of that milestone without a separate command
acceptance: a created checkpoint manifest contains every named field and its journalSequence equals the sequence of the last event read when it was created
creating a checkpoint with a name that already exists for that project is refused and records nothing
checkpoint.list returns the checkpoints of that project only, oldest first
a checkpoint manifest is derived from the event log, not from a second state store
re-reading a checkpoint returns exactly the recorded manifest

features.title: The deterministic recovery packet
features.outcome: A fresh worker can continue recorded work from a recovery packet that names the current task, the accepted baseline, surviving candidate artifacts, completed actions, unresolved effects, failed checks, remaining work and the remaining allowance. It is assembled deterministically, without a model, and carries no private model reasoning and no role transcript.
features.scope: New module src/progressdesk/recovery.py and the route table in src/progressdesk/runtime.py. Read the event log and the artifact store only.
interfaces: route verb 'recovery.packet' with params project_id and optional checkpoint_id -> packet with keys projectId, checkpointId, currentTask, acceptedBaseline, survivingCandidateArtifacts, completedActions, unresolvedEffects, failedChecks, remainingWork, allowance
acceptance: the packet names the current task and the remaining allowance
the packet lists the accepted artifact references and the surviving candidate artifacts
no raw role transcript or private reasoning appears in the packet
the same checkpoint and project produce an identical packet
building the packet records no model or tool execution

features.title: One start operation that reconciles before it dispatches
features.outcome: First start and restart are the same project.start operation. It takes the project lifecycle lock, reads the last valid checkpoint and the events after it, asks the register which recorded jobs are still alive, rebuilds the workspace from accepted artefacts while keeping unaccepted work as salvage, and either establishes a clean execution boundary or returns a typed outcome and dispatches nothing. A healthy existing run is returned as it stands instead of being duplicated.
features.scope: Only src/progressdesk/runtime.py, src/progressdesk/broker.py and the route table. Do not change the event vocabulary, the definition pipeline or the milestone gate.
interfaces: route verb 'project.start' with params project_id, request_id -> the GO record plus {'reconciliation': {'reconciled': [...], 'removed': [...], 'blockers': [...]}}
a typed outcome 'recovery_blocked' with evidence when the scene cannot be made clean
the lifecycle lock is identity checked, so a stale lock is distinguishable from a live one
acceptance: starting a project with no registered jobs reports nothing to remove and no blocker
a registered job that is gone from the operating system is reported as removed, not as running
a torn final event record is recovered and the recovery is recorded
an interior corruption of the event log is reported as a blocker and no work is dispatched
calling project.start twice does not create a second controller for the project
the start records no model, tool or provider execution of its own

features.title: The log is read in the order it was written
features.outcome: The event log is read in the order it was written. The numbering is a coordinate, not a proof: a gap in it is not an error, and the log does not refuse to open over one. A duplicate event id with different content is still refused, because that is one fact claimed twice.
interfaces: the reader orders the events and returns them, with no rule about the spacing of the numbers
a repeated event id with identical content is folded into one event
acceptance: a log with a gap in the numbering opens and reads in order
a repeated event id with different content is refused
a torn final record is still left for the housekeeping to repair

features.title: Any non-delivery enters the split ladder
features.outcome: A feature that does not deliver is split, and split again, until it is delivered or unsplittable. The cause of the non-delivery is the splitter's evidence, not a reason to stop: a feature that was too large for one attempt is exactly the case the split is for.
interfaces: a round that ends without a delivery enters the split path
a capacity refusal is not a work outcome and pauses instead
acceptance: a round that was cut off short is split rather than abandoned
a split that is applied leaves two ordinary features in the plan
a feature that cannot be split ends in the towel

features.title: A round that changed nothing is a delivery
features.outcome: A builder that reports success and changed nothing has still delivered: the feature is present in the room as it stands, and the room's state is the delivery. A feature that was already implemented must not be impossible to deliver.
interfaces: a successful round with no changed files freezes the room's state as the candidate
acceptance: a successful round that changed nothing records a candidate and closes as a delivery
the assembly contains the room's state
a round that changed files still delivers only those files
